title: Chef John's Nashville Hot Chicken
description: This Nashville hot chicken recipe featuring ultra-crispy fiery fried chicken with a spicy glaze is one of the most amazing fried chicken dishes you will ever taste!
ingredients: 1 cup vegetable oil for frying, or as needed

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Place chicken pieces in a large bowl.

Whisk buttermilk, pickle brine, hot sauce, and egg together in a bowl; pour over chicken and stir to ensure each piece is thoroughly coated. Cover and marinate chicken in the refrigerator 2 to 4 hours.

Combine flour and fine salt in a shallow flat dish. Remove chicken from marinade; blot with paper towels. Reserve marinade. Toss chicken in flour until thoroughly coated. Return chicken to marinade, coating all sides; remove chicken from marinade allowing excess to drip back into the bowl. Toss chicken again in flour mixture; place on a rack. Set aside at room temperature to allow coating to dry out a bit, about 15 minutes.

Place butter and lard in a large pot; add cayenne pepper, brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, kosher salt, and black pepper. Place over medium-high heat; cook and stir until fats melt. Remove from heat; keep sauce warm.

Fill a cast-iron skillet about ⅓ of the way with vegetable oil. Heat oil to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) over medium-high heat. Carefully place chicken into hot oil, skin-sides down. Maintain an oil temperature of 325 degrees F (165 degrees C), adjusting heat as needed. Fry until an instant read thermometer inserted into thickest parts, near but not touching bones, reads 165 degrees F (74 degrees C), 8 to 10 minutes per side.
Transfer chicken to a rack to drain. Brush both sides with sauce, stirring the sauce first if separation occurs—this is normal due to the melted fats.

video.description: Experience Nashville’s culinary heat in this extra-crispy fried chicken doused in a fiery cayenne glaze. Chicken pieces soak in a buttermilk marinade that also includes pickle brine and Louisiana hot sauce for extra kick. Double dredging lends that all-important crunch in the fryer, but what you’ll remember once this chicken is served on white bread with bread and butter pickles is a hot, hot sauce of cayenne, butter, lard, brown sugar, paprika and garlic. Fire away!
